title: Translated anticoncentration bound
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set and let $X:\Omega\to\mathbb R$ have uniform mean zero and uniform $L^2$ norm one. Suppose $\rho>0$ and, for every $a,b\in\mathbb R$, the uniform $L^4$ norm of $x\mapsto a+\rho bX(x)$ is at most the uniform $L^2$ norm of $x\mapsto a+bX(x)$. For $\theta\in\mathbb R$ and $0<t<1$, the uniform probability that $|X(x)-\theta|>t$ is at least $\left(\frac{\rho^2(1-t^2)+\rho^2\theta^2}{1+\rho^2\theta^2}\right)^2$.
hypotheses_covered: The stated uniform $L^4$-to-$L^2$ contraction holds for all real $a,b$
